newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to permit scrap metal exports from 1997.
newsitem.headline: Israel to permit scrap metal exports from 1997.

text.p: Israel's Industry and Trade Ministry said on Monday it would permit scrap-metal exports for the first time starting in January 1997.

Ministry Director-General Joshua Gleitman said the current ban had been imposed to protect the profitability of domestic steelmakers, among them United Steel Works, a subsidiary of Koor Industries. The government feared that a completely open market would have raised Israeli scrap metal prices because of competition from foreign buyers.

However, Gleitman said, the low prices for scrap resulting from the ban had discouraged scrap collection, which was harming the environment. In addition, Israel is required under its free trade area (FTA) agreement with the European Union to open up its scrap market, the ministry noted.

As compensation to the local steel industry, Gleitman said the ministry would step up measures to prevent the dumping of imported steel. He said the ministry was completing an investigation of dumping charges by European makers and said a decision on whether to impose sanctions would be made in the next several days.
